title: A skeleton of $\Dctf$ is a set of compact generators
statement: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, a field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with $q$ elements, and an algebraic closure $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of $k_0$, the global finite-field datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$. Let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] ([def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. The admissible commutative condensed coefficient rings $\Lambda$ here are: the condensation of a finite discrete commutative ring $A$ annihilated by a power of $\ell$; the condensations of $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E$ with their $\ell$-adic topologies [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]; and the ring $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}}_\ell$ of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], whose sections on a profinite set $S$ are the continuous maps $S\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with image contained in one finite subextension. Write $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]; in the last case this is exactly [def-sfb-qlbar-coefficient-ring]. Write $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ for the module-object category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and put $\mathcal T=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$, its ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All small sets and coproducts use [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)\subseteq\mathcal T$ be the bounded constructible finite-Tor-amplitude category [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. In this statement $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ is the full subcategory of this fixed $\mathcal T$ obtained by intersecting all full replete triangulated subcategories [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] containing $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and closed under its ambient small coproducts, as in [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](2). Let $G$ be a small skeleton of $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, that is, a set of representatives of its isomorphism classes. Every object of $G$ is compact [def-pc-compact-object] in $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$. If $K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ satisfies $\Hom(C[n],K)=0$ for every $C\in G$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$ (shifts as in [def-weil-triangulated-category]), then $K$ is isomorphic to the zero object.

proof.text: For a finite discrete canonical ring use finiteCompactProEtale and ambient coproduct closure. Pull the given ring-object isomorphism to X. The new coefficient-isomorphism lemma carries Dctf into the canonical Dctf. Minimality carries its localizing closure into the canonical closure. The exact fully faithful derived restriction preserves coproducts, and the square of canonical direct-sum Hom maps commutes on every summand; all other edges are bijective. This reflects compactness to the original coefficients.

For rational canonical coefficients use the internal compactness clause of constructible_compactness in Loc(Dbc). The inclusion Dctf subset Dbc induces an inclusion of localizing closures by minimality; all small coproducts of the latter closure are ambient. An explicit full-subcategory coproduct comparison identifies the two Hom maps. For integral canonical coefficients choose the nonnegative Ext bounds from integralConstructibleExt, establish CharP for the fixed algebraic closure using the cardinality of its finite base, and apply integralConstructibleCompactness. Use the same full-subcategory comparison and coefficient-isomorphism reflection as in step 1. The bottom finite subextension is isometrically isomorphic to Q_l, and its integer ring to Z_l, giving explicit continuous-function condensed-ring isomorphisms for both base cases.

For generation take the left orthogonal of the shift closure of the singleton K. Mathlib makes it replete and triangulated. The coproduct universal property makes it closed under every existing ambient coproduct. The shift adjunction and the supplied representative isomorphisms put every Dctf object in this orthogonal. By the defining intersection, K belongs too, so its identity is zero. IsZero.isoZero gives the required isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Compactness; scalar isomorphism invariance made explicit

split_report.blueprint: Steps 1-3 realize Compactness in sk-lem-brown-hypotheses-generation.proof.md, retaining the finite/integral/rational route; steps 4-7 realize Generation, explicitly proving closure of the orthogonal class under shifts, cones and small coproducts before applying minimality. tool_uses.why: Generic theorem for ANY condensed ring: provides the localizing closure, ambient sums and minimality for the exact chapter coefficient object, without importing sk-def-localizing-closure's conflicting Qbar coefficient convention.
Definition of compactness used in the statement; it introduces no alternate proof route.
Generic shift equivalence and TR1-TR3 axioms used to prove cone closure explicitly; the unit does not restate these axioms.
Clause (2) for the integral coefficient ring O_E only, as required by the unit compactness step; no Qbar coefficient change is taken from this statement.

Only its explicit rational ctf=Dbc assertion (4) is used for the chapter coefficient objects; the same identification prescribed by the Brown unit, without deriving ambient compactness from a 2-colimit.

Clause (3) places the generically defined rational localizing closure in Dic with the exact current condensed coefficients, so the displayed Hom/direct-sum assertion in the unit-prescribed rational compactness theorem applies without using its stale closure-definition reference.
